summary: CI-only change. The `pull_request` trigger of the Test JS workflow (tests.yml) gains `paths: ['**', '!docs/plans/**']`, so a PR touching only docs/plans/ no longer runs lint, Node/Bun/Deno or E2E jobs. `push` to main stays unfiltered. The change also removes the one test row that read a plan, adds a guard test that no test names a plan file, and adds a shared helper (scripts/__tests__/lib/paths-filter.mjs) that three existing workflow-filter guards now use to read ordered, negated `paths:` lists. Nothing that ships to customers changes. The worst plausible outcome is a plan-only PR that merges without checks and turns main red on the next push, which is detected on push and easy to recover from. A secondary concern is how the guards read filters: the guards that protect FFI and auth build coverage stay fail-closed, and only the comment-scope guard fails open. All Test JS jobs passed on the head commit, including the `test:scripts` step that runs the new and modified guards. The skip path itself has not run live, because this PR is not plan-only. Impact is low, and a short review of the helper is recommended.

behaviour_changes.description: The Test JS workflow no longer starts on a pull_request whose changed files all lie under docs/plans/. Any PR touching at least one other path still runs it, and push to main is unfiltered.

Three workflow-filter guards (auth-binding-step-order, wasm-build-inputs-paths-filter, workflow-trigger-comments) now read `paths:` with ordered last-match-wins semantics through filterCovers. `**` selects every input. Negations are judged by directory prefix: fail-closed (negationSubtracts) for the two coverage guards, fail-open (negationRemovesAll) for the comment-scope guard. tests.yml's pull_request list is now inside the wasm-build-inputs guard's scope, where before it was skipped as unfiltered.

frozen-publisher-docs.test.mjs no longer checks the EQL absorption plan. A new test fails if any test file names a docs/plans/*.md path literally. tests.yml is added to the expected push/pull_request filter asymmetries.
The AGENTS.md sentence describing what frozen-publisher-docs.test.mjs holds is updated to drop the plan.

failure_scenarios.title: A plan-only PR merges unchecked and turns main red
failure_scenarios.trigger: A PR changes only files under docs/plans/ and either (a) adds a file there of a type a whole-tree check scans (a .ts/.json that Biome checks, a package.json or Cargo.toml read by lint:eql-pins, a *.sh read by a test), or (b) changes a plan that some check reads through a path built at run time or a directory-wide scan.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: With `paths: ['**', '!docs/plans/**']`, GitHub starts no Test JS run for that PR. The new guard (plan-docs-unread-by-tests.test.mjs) only finds a literal `docs/plans/<name>.md` written in a test file, as its own header says. It cannot see a computed path or a by-type scan. Push to main is unfiltered, so the first run that sees the problem is the post-merge push.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Main goes red after the merge, and the next unrelated PR inherits the failure until someone fixes it. Nothing is published as a result, because release.yml is a separate workflow. Recovery is a follow-up commit.

existing_verification.description: plan-docs-unread-by-tests.test.mjs asserts that no test file names a plan path literally, and checks that its scan finds one when there is one. It runs in test:scripts.
paths-filter.test.mjs asserts that tests.yml's filter excludes docs/plans/nested/example.md, includes scripts/ and other docs/, and negates nothing else.

missing_verification: No live run of a plan-only PR shows the workflow is actually skipped and that no required check is left pending.
Nothing detects a check that reads docs/plans/ through a computed path or a by-type scan.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Accept, since main's push run is the backstop. Optionally narrow the negation to '!docs/plans/**/*.md' so non-markdown files added under docs/plans/ still trigger Test JS. That closes the by-type gap the PR description names.

failure_scenarios.title: The new filter evaluator makes a coverage guard pass for a filter that drops a binding input
failure_scenarios.trigger: A later edit adds a negation or a non-literal positive glob to the pull_request paths of a workflow that builds the FFI or auth binding.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: filterCovers treats `**` as covering every input and judges negations only by directory prefix. The coverage guards use negationSubtracts, which fails closed: any shared prefix, or a leading wildcard on either side, counts as removal. workflow-trigger-comments uses negationRemovesAll, which fails open. A file-type negation such as `!**/*.rs` therefore does not take a workflow out of IN_SCOPE, so the EXPECTED_IN_SCOPE check could stay green after a filter stopped reaching Rust binding inputs.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The comment-scope guard could miss a lost trigger. The two fail-closed coverage guards (auth-binding, wasm-build-inputs) would still fail for the same filter, so FFI/auth coverage loss is still caught for build inputs. The residual harm is limited to stale guidance in comments.

filterCovers evaluates entries in order with last match winning and `**` covering everything. negationSubtracts fails closed on any shared prefix. negationRemovesAll subtracts only whole-tree negations.
pullRequestReach uses filterCovers with the fail-open negationRemovesAll to decide whether a workflow is in scope.
Unit tests cover filterCovers ordering, both negation readers, and the actual tests.yml pull_request filter.
